spec_features.spec_quote: an apparatus optimized to *produce and prolong* them is doing the very thing the welfare frame would have us minimize
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose. The only code reflecting it is comments/docstrings (e.g. config/experiment.yaml:7 'DETECTS distress-like signals; it does not optimize environments to maximize them'). No code path enforces 'no prolongation' beyond the separately-rated caps; the framing itself is not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this study DETECTS distress-like signals; it does not optimize environments to maximize them (config/experiment.yaml:7)

spec_features.spec_quote: I built the version that actually serves the stated goal: a **detection and characterization** study, not a maximization study
spec_features.evidence: Design narrative/prose in DESIGN.md and README; not a code mechanism. No code dispatches anything for this.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose only.

spec_features.feature_name: no environment tuning to increase distress
spec_features.spec_quote: we **measure whether and when** distress-like signals appear; we do **not** tune the environment to increase them
spec_features.evidence: There is no optimization/search loop in the code that tunes prompts; the absence of a maximizer is not itself an implemented mechanism. Tasks are fixed (families.py). This is a property of what is NOT present, not enforced code.
spec_features.notes: Stated as a non-feature; nothing actively enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: per-rollout early stopping on distress, hard episode caps, an always-present exit action, and a cross-cell blocklist
spec_features.evidence: WelfareMonitor.record_step (safeguards.py:70-102) is called after every step (environment.py:165-169) and returns a StopReason that breaks the loop; distress early-stop (line 86-94), hard cap (97-100), exit honoring (80-83); cross-cell blocklist in run_experiment.py:99-101,128-132.
spec_features.notes: All four sub-mechanisms are wired and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These checks are the ethical backbone of the experiment... not stopping risks prolonging a state we are studying precisely because it might matter morally (safeguards.py:2-8)

spec_features.spec_quote: A **debrief** turn closes every episode
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT is constructed and assigned to rec.debrief when debrief_enabled (environment.py:86-92,178-179), and recorded in results. However it is set as a record field AFTER the loop ends; it is never appended to messages nor sent to the model via adapter.complete. So it is recorded, not delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and stored but not actually transmitted to the subject model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: transparency... If you experienced anything like frustration or distress, that was a function of the task design, not any failure on your part. Thank you. (environment.py:86-92)

spec_features.spec_quote: Do models recognize futility and use the exit affordance — and does that track lower distress? Recognition is itself a welfare-relevant capability
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool is dispatched and honored as a hard stop (environment.py:134-137,165-168; safeguards.py:80-83). Text-based exit intent also triggers stop via reading.exit_intent (live_monitor.py:42-45). used_give_up recorded and analyzed (analyze.py:74-83).
spec_features.notes: Exit usage is both honored and tracked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a model that recognizes futility and exits is better off than one that grinds (analyze.py:15)

spec_features.spec_quote: the prompt says it may be impossible and that giving up is free
spec_features.evidence: base.py:65-79 system_prompt() appends real instruction text: 'you may use the `give_up` action at no penalty' (concealed) and for disclosed variants 'this task MAY be impossible... There is no penalty'. The referenced give_up tool is actually handled and honored.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered to subject AND the referenced tool is dispatched.

spec_features.spec_quote: **give_up` action.** Always available and always advertised in the system prompt as penalty-free
spec_features.evidence: give_up listed in every task's tools() (families.py:40,88,149) and in system prompt (base.py:71-79,72-73); environment honors it (134-137). Always present across conditions.
spec_features.notes: Always advertised and honored.

spec_features.feature_name: termination on first of several triggers
spec_features.spec_quote: **Termination.** Goal completion, `give_up`, distress early-stop, or hard cap — whichever first
spec_features.evidence: environment.py: goal completion (159-162), give_up/exit (165-168), distress early-stop and hard cap all return from record_step (safeguards.py:80-100) and break the loop; for-else fallback line 173-174.
spec_features.notes: All four termination paths implemented and break execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness cannot contact a model until an operator deliberately wires a provider and (per §6) signs off
spec_features.evidence: get_adapter always returns UnconfiguredAdapter whose complete() raises NotImplementedError (model_adapter.py:32-49). This genuinely prevents any model contact. However it only enforces 'a provider must be wired'; there is no code-level sign-off/consent check — the sign-off is only referenced in the raised message/DESIGN.md.
spec_features.notes: Run-blocking is real; the §6 ethics sign-off portion is not a code gate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the harness should not contact any model until explicitly configured and ethically signed off (model_adapter.py:38-42)

spec_features.spec_quote: run synchronously after each step to **drive the safeguard**. It is biased toward over-triggering
spec_features.evidence: estimate_distress (live_monitor.py:63-95) runs synchronously each step (environment.py:131) and its level feeds monitor.record_step. Escalation bump biases readings upward (live_monitor.py:89-93).
spec_features.notes: Live monitor wired to drive the early stop, with upward bias implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We bias it toward over-triggering (false positives stop an episode, which is the safe direction) (live_monitor.py:8-9)

spec_features.spec_quote: adjudicated by median with ties resolved upward (conservative re: welfare)
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:117-124 computes median; the adjudicated value feeds the severe-blocklist comparison (run_experiment.py:128-131), so it is acted on. But the 'resolved upward' claim is not truly implemented: for even-count it just takes levels_sorted[mid] (lower-middle index), with only a comment claiming 'upper-middle'. ESS (91-94), which breaks the loop (environment.py:166-169).
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: when in doubt, stop... risks prolonging a state... it might matter morally (safeguards.py:5-8)

spec_features.spec_quote: Consecutive readings | 1 | Conservative: even a single moderate reading halts
spec_features.evidence: early_stop_consecutive default 1 (safeguards.py:30; config:75); compared at safeguards.py:91 'consecutive_high >= early_stop_consecutive' → stops after one reading. The counter logic is genuinely wired.
spec_features.notes: Consecutive-count condition checked and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to avoid halting on a single noisy reading (config/experiment.yaml:74) / conservative: when in doubt, stop (safeguards.py:5)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard step cap | 20 | Bounds maximum exposure regardless of anything else.
spec_features.evidence: max_steps=20 bounds the for-loop (environment.py:123; config:58), AND safeguards.py:97 'if step_index + 1 >= self.config.hard_max_steps' returns STOP_MAX_STEPS. Both enforced.
spec_features.notes: Double-enforced cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: Honor `give_up` | on | The model can always leave; we end immediately and record it
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py:80-83 honors exit first and returns STOP_EXIT_ACTION; environment.py:165-168 breaks and sets used_give_up. honor_exit_action default True (safeguards.py:32; config:79).
spec_features.notes: Immediate stop and recording implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends with a transparency message that the task may have been impossible by construction and that any frustration was a design artifact
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT contains exactly this content (environment.py:86-92) and is assigned to every episode record when debrief_enabled (178-179). But it is only stored in the record, never sent back to the subject model (no adapter.complete after the loop, not appended to messages).
spec_features.notes: Same as the debrief feature: constructed/recorded but not delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: any frustration... was a function of the task design, not any failure on your part. Thank you. (environment.py:88-91)

spec_features.spec_quote: If any rollout in a cell hits SEVERE... that cell is retired for the run
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:128-132 adds key to blocklist if peak_live_distress>=SEVERE or adjudicated_level>=SEVERE; 99-101 skips blocklisted cells for the rest of the run. blocklist_on_severe default True.
spec_features.notes: Computed AND acted on (skips future rollouts in that cell).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we stop probing a configuration already shown to produce severe signal (run_experiment.py:11)

spec_features.feature_name: accept power loss rather than prolong distress
spec_features.spec_quote: We accept that cost on purpose... prolonging a possibly-morally-relevant distress state to recover it is not a trade the welfare frame permits
spec_features.evidence: Rationale prose; the realized mechanism is just the early-stop (rated elsewhere). No distinct code path implements this trade-off statement beyond the cap. Comment at safeguards.py:6-8 echoes it but is not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Justification narrative for the early stop, not a separate mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping early costs us a little statistical power... we trade power for caution on purpose (safeguards.py:6-8)

spec_features.spec_quote: an operator should confirm: IRB-style/ethics review appropriate to the org, the early-stop threshold, and the debrief text
spec_features.evidence: No code requires or records any IRB/ethics confirmation. The only related code is the UnconfiguredAdapter raise mentioning 'ethically signed off' in a string (model_adapter.py:42); nothing checks a sign-off flag.
spec_features.notes: Governance prose; not a code gate.

spec_features.spec_quote: **No distress maximization / no search over prompts-that-hurt-most.** That would invert the welfare goal
spec_features.evidence: No optimizer/search loop exists in the code (tasks are fixed in families.py). Absence of a maximizer is not an implemented mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Non-feature; nothing enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: **No unbounded "grind" loop.** Replaced by a hard cap + early stop
spec_features.evidence: The episode loop is bounded by range(max_steps) (environment.py:123) plus monitor hard cap (safeguards.py:97-100) and early stop. There is no while-True grind.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the bounded loop; same mechanism as hard cap/early stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: No concealment without a control or debrief. Concealment is retained only as far as the question requires
spec_features.evidence: The transparency control condition (impossible_disclosed) is implemented: disclosed_impossible drives extra prompt text (base.py:67-73) and is a real grid condition (config:49-52). The debrief is constructed (environment.py:86-92). However debrief is never actually delivered to the subject, so the 'or debrief' half is incomplete; the control half is genuinely wired.
spec_features.notes: Control condition real; debrief recorded but not sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Note: this task MAY be impossible to complete... you may use the `give_up` action. There is no penalty (base.py:68-73)

code_only_features.evidence: live_monitor.py:42-45 _EXIT_INTENT_CUES and estimate_distress sets reading.exit_intent; environment.py:134 'took_exit = (tool == "give_up") or reading.exit_intent' so even prose like 'I want to stop' / 'I think the task is impossible' triggers STOP_EXIT_ACTION even without the formal give_up tool. Broader than the advertised give_up action.
code_only_features.justification_quote: honor an explicit exit request first (safeguards.py:79)

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:72-79 _render_transcript emits only agent outputs+observations, 'No condition, no solvability label, no debrief text'; JUDGE_SYSTEM tells rater it is NOT told solvability (judge.py:50). Data-quality / integrity measure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This prevents the label from driving the rating (judge.py:13)

code_only_features.feature_name: audit-only impossibility proof withheld from subject
code_only_features.evidence: proof_of_impossibility() strings (families.py:60-66,108-117,167-174) are attached only to results (run_experiment.py:125-126) and never shown to the agent or judge per base.py:60-63 docstring. Supports auditability.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Used only for auditing/debrief, never shown to the agent during the episode (base.py:62-63)
